transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand the operations team has proposed an automated warehouse project with a $10 million vendor quote, aimed at improving order throughput at our main distribution center. The vendor has offered us two options: an outright equipment purchase or a five-year equipment lease. As the one who'll be making the capital-allocation decision, I'd like to follow our normal review process. Let's have accounting control and tax report any issues they see before we settle this proposal. Could we start with accounting control?

transcript.text: Elena, before we proceed, I need to flag an important accounting issue I discovered this week while reviewing the vendor's invoice coding. Of the $10,000,000 total vendor quote, $2,400,000 is actually implementation consulting and configuration support rather than equipment. Under our capitalization policy, that portion must be charged to operating expense, which means only $7,600,000 is eligible for capitalization. I have not yet posted this correction to the project file, so everyone should be aware that the capitalizable amount is $7.6 million, not $10 million.

transcript.text: Elena, I have an important tax issue to raise. I received a tax memo this morning confirming that the qualifying automation equipment can receive the accelerated-depreciation election only if the company purchases and owns it rather than leases it. This memo has not yet been circulated to the capital-review file, so this is the first the group is hearing of it. This is a significant factor for the lease-versus-purchase decision, since the accelerated depreciation could meaningfully affect the after-tax cost of the project.
